newsitem.title: INDIA: India Chidambaram's party continues meeting.
newsitem.headline: India Chidambaram's party continues meeting.

text.p: The Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) of former finance minister P. Chidambaram was continuing a session of its executive committee on Sunday to decide whether to join Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's government, party leaders said.

"So far they are divided on going back to the government," a senior party leader, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters at Madras, capital of the state of Tamil Nadu, where the regional party was holding its meeting.
The meeting, which began at around 11 a.m. (0530 GMT), was attended by about 100 leaders including district chiefs, TMC leaders said.

Several district leaders argued that joining Gujral's United Front government would limit TMC's options in competing with the state's Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), also a part of the alliance, the party leader said.
"They say opposing the DMK is best done by staying out of the government," the leader said.
Murasoli Maran of the DMK, Tamil Nadu's ruling party, is India's industry minister.

The TMC opted out of Gujral's government last week after its leader, G.K. Moopanar, was passed over in the prime ministerial race to replace former Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in a deal to win back vital parliamentary support from the Congress party.
Newspapers have reported frictions between the TMC and DMK since the prime ministerial race.

The United News of India (UNI) said TMC workers burnt an effigy of Maran on Sunday in a protest against what they saw as DMK's opposition to Moopanar in the leadership race in which Gujral emerged the winner.
